title: Who gets the exception each time
question: On which payees do different kinds of exception fall in different years: no competition one year, approval after the fact the next, an amendment after that?
finding: 52 payees drew three or more different kinds of exception spread over four or more of the eight fiscal years; 17 drew at least one in every year. Together they were paid $6.25 billion, $1.73 billion of it under rules that set competition aside; 45 are nonprofits and 47 carry warning signs elsewhere. At the top: Tenderloin Housing Clinic Inc (5 kinds over 8 years); Healthright 360 (5 kinds over 8 years); Community Housing Partnership (5 kinds over 8 years); Felton Institute (5 kinds over 7 years); Homeless Prenatal Program (5 kinds over 7 years). The exceptions screens count how many kinds stack on each supplier; this one shows the order they came in.
how: Six kinds of exception are dated by fiscal year 2019 to 2026. From the payment file: $25,000 or more paid in the year under emergency powers, as sole source, under an ordinance that waives bidding, or under another "not bid" rule; the year is the one the payment was issued in, read from its voucher number. From the Board’s files (by date of introduction, passed files only): an agreement approved after the fact, an amendment that extends or raises an agreement, and titles that state a sole-source or emergency award. A payee is listed with three or more kinds over four or more years, not all first seen in the same year. Ranked by kinds times years, then by money under no-competition rules. The column from the exceptions screens gives that file’s own count of kinds, which uses contracts and two further tests.
limits: A large provider of homelessness, mental-health or pandemic services meets several because of its field: the Board waived bidding for that work, the pandemic put it under emergency rules, and long agreements are amended as needs grow. The timeline shows that exceptions recur for the same payee; it does not show that any was unjustified. Board counterparties are text-mined and matched by name. What would settle a row: the justification memo for each exception in turn, and whether the same reason was given each year. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. The $992.6 million of outside spending that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier is in none of the figures here; it is used only to tell that a payee is not new. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
